# Maria del Mar Torrente (Mar Torrente) — Digital Entertainment Design Engineer

> Colombian Digital Entertainment Design Engineer and multidisciplinary artist: rigging, procedural animation, 3D animation, game design, programming, and interactive experiences. Producer and visual director of the award-winning animated short Platillo; creator of Regret, a 2D short with 1M+ YouTube views made solo at age 17. Portfolio website: https://estorrente.github.io/Portfolio/

## Highlights
- Outstanding Student of the Digital Entertainment Design Engineering program (IDED), Universidad Pontificia Bolivariana, 2026.
- "Best DEX Project" won 3 times (2026‑01, 2025‑02, 2024‑02), i.e. her team's project was named the program's best project in three different semesters.
- Platillo (13-min interactive animated mystery, producer & visual director) won three awards in 2026: Best DEX Project, Excellence in Visual Design, Most Original Visual Style.
- Greatest Social / Cultural Impact award (2025-1).
- Regret: 9-minute 2D animated short made entirely solo at 17, 1M+ views on YouTube.
- Builds custom character rigs from scratch (no autorig) with procedural animation, facial systems and custom tools (Blender, Maya, Harmony).
- Leads multidisciplinary teams and production pipelines; comfortable moving between the creative and the technical.

## About
- I'm a Colombian Engineer in Design for Digital Entertainment and a multidisciplinary artist working across 3D art, animation, rigging, illustration, programming, and interactive experiences.
- My work ranges from custom character rigs and procedural animation systems to animated films, educational games, and interactive projects. I've worked across the full animation pipeline (from concept and storyboarding through modelling, rigging, animation, rendering, editing, and compositing) and I'm comfortable learning new tools whenever a project demands it.
- One of my biggest strengths is adaptability. I'm comfortable being the person who says, “I don't know how to do this yet. Let me figure it out.”
- That mindset has taken me from character animation to rigging, procedural systems, shaders, VR, game design, programming, interactive storytelling, and production management.
- I've also led multidisciplinary teams and production pipelines throughout university, with projects receiving three Best Project awards, a Social & Cultural Impact award, an Excellence in Visual Design award, and the Outstanding Student award for my degree.
- Outside university, my independent animated short Regret, produced entirely by me at 17, surpassed 1 million views on YouTube.
- I enjoy being somewhere between the creative and the technical: understanding how something should feel, figuring out how it needs to work, and building whatever systems are necessary to get there.
- I don't always know how to build something when I start. That's usually where things get interesting.

## Skills & tools
- Core skills: Project Management, Rigging, 3D Animation, Experience Design, Emotional Storytelling, Creative Direction.
- Software: Blender, Maya, Harmony, Unity, MotionBuilder, After Effects.
- Currently learning: Houdini, Moho, Advanced Simulations, Unreal Engine.

## Featured projects
- **Platillo** — Interactive Animated Mystery · Producer · Visual Director. A 13-minute interactive mystery combining animation, puzzle mechanics, character-driven storytelling, and a stylized 3D production pipeline. Watch: https://youtu.be/fdkMMAWzWsQ
- **StarBlitz** — Educational virtual world · Game Design · Programming · 2D/3D Art · Project Management. An educational virtual world that teaches children to recognize grooming and unsafe situations by practicing real decisions and seeing their consequences, instead of being given warnings. Watch: https://youtu.be/xijbo6FrxBQ
- **Regret** — 9-Minute 2D Animated Short · Solo Production. A 9-minute animated short I created independently at 17, taking the project from concept to final delivery, and eventually reaching more than one million views on YouTube. Watch: https://youtu.be/fDQSp0BcJGo
- **Crónicas del Tonusco** — Augmented Reality Museum Experience · Concept · Project Lead · Programming. An approximately 40-minute augmented reality experience in which visitors of the Juan del Corral Museum scan real objects to trigger animated scenes that place them back into their historical and cultural context.

## Rigging (https://estorrente.github.io/Portfolio/#/rigging)
- **Eridan** (BLENDER): My first fully custom character rig, built entirely from scratch without an autorig. I designed the system around animator-friendly workflows, combining expressive facial controls, procedural animation, custom tools, interchangeable clothing, and a stylized NPR rendering pipeline.
- **Golub** (BLENDER): A custom rig for an intentionally awkward pigeon, designed to turn repetitive locomotion and flight animation into simple, animator-friendly controls.
- **Skirt** (BLENDER): A custom deformation system developed to solve a common character-animation problem: keeping a skirt flexible and visually clean while preventing it from clipping through the legs.
- **Biped Character** (MAYA): A character-rigging study focused on deformation quality, weight painting, and building a reliable animation-ready setup using Maya's autorig workflow.
- **Dragon** (MAYA): A customizable dragon rig built around procedural relationships and driven-key systems, allowing the character's proportions and wing behavior to be adjusted without rebuilding the setup.
- **Excavator** (MAYA): A mechanical rig designed to feel like a small toy vehicle, with procedural track movement and intuitive controls for operating the excavator.
- **Hand** (MAYA): A compact rigging study exploring how complex hand movement can be simplified into a small set of animator-friendly attributes.
- **Aria** (HARMONY): A Harmony character rig developed as part of my 2D animation work.

## Animation (https://estorrente.github.io/Portfolio/#/animation)
- **Platillo: Intro**: The opening sequence of Platillo, a 13-minute interactive animated mystery. I contributed across the entire production pipeline, from character creation and rigging to animation, visual direction, and production coordination.
- **Platillo: Evidence 4, Hugo**: A character-animation sequence from Platillo, taking Hugo from model to final performance through modelling, rigging, and animation.
- **Akali vs Gru**: An animation study focused on understanding why a scene works, not simply reproducing its final poses.

## 3D modelling (https://estorrente.github.io/Portfolio/#/modelling)
- **Granny**: A character created by translating a real person into a stylized fictional design, combining anatomical observation with costume, shape language, and character development.
- **Aragorn**: A character sculpt built completely from scratch, focused on anatomy, proportions, facial structure, and translating a recognizable character into a 3D form.
- **Low-Poly Astronaut**: A lightweight character designed for real-time VR, balancing visual clarity, stylized design, and performance constraints.
- **Eri: Base Mesh**: A reusable character base mesh designed with future sculpting, rigging, animation, and deformation in mind.
- **Steampunk Cat**: A stylized character combining organic anatomy with mechanical design, developed through shape language, costume, and visual storytelling.
